Paper · 2026-03-16

All five nucleobases found in asteroid Ryugu (Koga, Oba, Takano, Naraoka et al.)

Koga, Oba, Takano, Naraoka et al. · Nature Astronomy 10:655-663

In a sentence

Ryugu, like Bennu, holds all five letters used in DNA and RNA.

In plain words

Japan's Hayabusa2 brought back grains of asteroid Ryugu. Uracil was found in them in 2023; this study now reports all five nucleobases, the 'letters' of DNA and RNA. Ryugu has roughly equal amounts of the two families of bases, unlike Bennu and the Orgueil meteorite, which lean one way. The balance tracks how much ammonia each body had, which hints that the bases formed by one shared chemistry under different local conditions.

Technical detail

Adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine and uracil in Ryugu samples. Purines and pyrimidines are near equal in Ryugu; Murchison is purine-rich; Bennu and Orgueil pyrimidine-rich. Across Ryugu, Bennu and Orgueil the purine-to-pyrimidine ratio correlates negatively with ammonia.

What we take from it

Planned test

A ratio-versus-ammonia trend is exactly the kind of relationship task #11 can extend into a sealed prediction for compounds not yet reported from returned samples.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
